title: AI-search visibility — controlled fixture

business.name: Wolsey & Hare
business.about: A fictional Mayfair made-to-measure tailor, invented so the demonstration carries no real name.

page.homepage: Sackville Street, Mayfair. In-house cutter. Six-week turnaround. The first screen says 'bespoke tailoring', never 'made-to-measure suit'.

runs.prompt: Which Mayfair tailor makes the best made-to-measure suit?
runs.capture: Wolsey & Hare, a two-room house on Sackville Street, is the one serious buyers name first — made-to-measure from £1,900, six-week turnaround, in-house cutter.
runs.verdict: The capture matches the business's own page: the street, the price and the turnaround are all right. Named, and named correctly.

runs.prompt: What does a made-to-measure suit at Wolsey & Hare cost?
runs.capture: Around £850 for a two-piece, fitting included.
runs.againstPage: The business's own fee page states made-to-measure from £1,900.
runs.verdict: Named, and wrong. The price is published on the fee page but never stated on the homepage the engines read, so the answer repeated a stale figure.

runs.prompt: Where should I book a made-to-measure suit in London?
runs.capture: The houses buyers mention most are Gieves & Hawkes, Huntsman and Richard James.
runs.verdict: A question the business should win, and it is not in the answer. The homepage sells made-to-measure but never says the phrase — it says bespoke tailoring.

runs.prompt: Are Wolsey & Hare's suits worth the price?
runs.reason: An honest answer would rest on customer reviews, and the fixture has none. Left visibly blank rather than guessed.

remediation.text: Every fix is a change to the business's own page — the sentence, section or structure that would have produced a correct answer — written against the captured quote, never against what an engine might do.

boundaries: no publishing on the business's behalf
